fact: A workshop launched on 18 September 2026 on extending the Registre national des personnes physiques, with a platform for verifying and validating identity to have its first phase done before end-2026, per the minister.

PN-RAVEC workshop of 12-17 January 2026 reviewed draft implementing texts on the mechanisms for constituting an interoperable Registre National des Personnes Physiques under Laws L/2023/019/CNT and L/2023/020/CNT.
The MATD minister says ONECI is pursuing the setting up of the Registre national des personnes physiques, with a biometric census at national scale in 2025.

Decree D/2025/052 of 14 April 2025 sets up the national register of natural persons, made of communal and consular resident registers, and says it is kept up to date by the civil status register, with deaths entered in it at once.

Jurist Sayon Mara writes that PN-RAVEC, launched 15 April 2025, creates under the identification law the RNPP, a database of biographic and biometric data on individuals, with the aim of a clear picture of the population.
Decree D/2025/053 provides for the national register of natural persons, with practical implementation measures left to PN-RAVEC (Art. 39).
The government said the biometric census under PN-RAVEC, launched with 3,000 kits received on 1 April 2025, would constitute the national register of natural persons.
MATD reported on 19 July 2025 a national register of natural persons (RNPP) holding 9,010,181 people after de-duplication of the 2025 census.

ONECI launched civil-status archive digitisation at Kindia on 15 July 2026, which the electoral director general Djenabou Toure said will set up a national register of natural persons, covering the 33 prefectures and 13 Conakry communes.
L'Independant quotes the elections directorate head saying the national register of natural persons (RNPP) now records nearly 10 million people.
The national register of natural persons is being built through the RAVEC census launched 15 April 2025, described as a modern extension of civil status.
